title: Dynamic entitlement rebalancing and invoice smoothing PRD
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Provide a safe, auditable system to rebalance unused plan entitlements across eligible accounts, smooth transient overage charges into predictable invoice adjustments, and expose controls for finance and customer success to approve or override automated adjustments.
background: Customers increasingly purchase committed plans with monthly or annual entitlements. We see many situations where month-to-month usage variability leads to spikes that cause short-term overage invoices and manual dispute volume. Finance and CS teams want a configurable, auditable mechanism to reallocate unused entitlements (within contractual bounds) and convert single-month overages into invoice adjustments or deferred charges under clearly defined rules. Current behavior: immediate overage billing and manual refunds/credits. This creates poor developer experience, surprise invoices, and operational overhead.
goals: Reduce customer-reported billing disputes related to transient overages by >= 40% in Q2 after rollout
Reduce manual credit/refund work for Finance/CS by >= 60% for eligible cases
Provide programmatic APIs and Console controls for entitlement rebalancing and invoice smoothing with full audit trail
Ensure changes respect plan terms and do not alter total billed revenue recognition beyond agreed policies
outcome_metrics: Billing disputes related to overage (count) — target: -40%
Manual credit/refund tickets opened by Finance/CS (count) — target: -60%
% of eligible overage amount processed via smoothing vs immediate invoice — target: >=75%
Time to resolve entitlement rebalancing request (median hours) — target: <24h
scope: In scope: Implement entitlement rebalancing rules engine that can shift unused monthly credits between related accounts or sub-accounts where contract permits
In scope: Invoice smoothing pipeline that converts a single billing-cycle overage into a deferred charge applied to the next invoice or into plan credit, based on configurable policies
In scope: Console UI for Finance/CS to preview proposed rebalances, approve/override, and audit actions
In scope: Public REST API endpoints for programmatic requests and webhook notifications for adjustments
Out of scope: Changes to subscription contracts or legal billing terms (legal/finance must approve separate amendments)
Out of scope: Annual entitlement true-ups (this PRD focuses on monthly smoothing and intra-term redistribution only)
Out of scope: Real-time per-request dynamic throttling behavior — this interacts with quota admission but is handled by separate runtime features
requirements: R1: Rules engine must support configurable eligibility predicates: plan family, customer tier, linked accounts, minimum retained entitlement percentage, and lookback windows
R2: Smoothing policies must support: (a) deferred charge to next invoice with amortization schedule, (b) conversion to plan credit, (c) partial invoice credit with remainder billed immediately
R3: All automated adjustments must be logged with immutability: timestamp, initiating rule, eligible usage amounts, pre- and post-adjustment balances, actor (system or CSR), and correlation id
R4: Console must include a review workflow: preview, approve, reject, and an ability to set escalations and auto-approve thresholds
R5: Exposed API must allow querying eligibility, simulate adjustment outcomes, and submit approval/override actions. API authentication uses existing billing service auth and honors RBAC
R6: The pipeline must produce accounting-friendly artifacts: invoice line items tagged with smoothing reason codes and metadata to allow reconciliation in ERP
R7: Safety guardrails: maximum rebalanced percentage per account per month (configurable, default 30%), maximum deferred window (configurable, default 1 month), and an opt-out flag per customer
R8: Tests: unit, integration with billing engine, end-to-end with Console, and QA data validating invoice outcomes for 50 sample accounts before rollout
R9: Backward compatibility: existing billing history and invoices must be unchanged; smoothing only affects future invoices and adds adjustment line items
R10: Monitoring: metrics and alerts for failed adjustments, high override rates (>5%), and reconciliation mismatches
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Demo walkthrough showing entitlement rebalancing flow in Console for a linked account group, with audit log entries present
AC2: API simulation returns deterministic projected invoice delta for 10 representative usage profiles matching QA dataset
AC3: Automated pipeline processes synthetic overage events and creates correct deferred charge entries in staging ERP connector with correct reason codes
AC4: Finance-run reconciliation for staged sample accounts shows zero net revenue leakage beyond configured amortization rules
AC5: Rollout test: feature enabled for 5 beta customers without any billing disputes or reconciliation errors for 2 consecutive billing cycles
AC6: Ability for CS to manually approve an adjustment within Console and see immediate outbound webhook notification and audit log
AC7: Safety guardrails validated: attempts to rebalance > configured cap are rejected and logged
AC8: Monitoring alerts fire on simulated failure scenarios and lead to created incident in oncall workflow
implementation_notes: Leverage existing billing-processor job queue and invoice model to attach 'smoothing' line items rather than rewriting historical invoices
Reuse RBAC roles and billing service auth; new permission 'billing:adjust' required for Console actions
Rules engine should be authored in a declarative format stored in Config Service to allow non-developer rule updates
Provide one-time migration script to tag existing linked accounts that are eligible for beta program
Coordinate with Legal and Finance to add reason codes and mapping documents for ERP integration
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design & security review (2 weeks) — finalize data model, reason codes, and legal sign-off
Phase 1: Implementation in staging (4 weeks) — rules engine, API, Console UX, and billing pipeline changes
Phase 2: Closed beta (2 billing cycles) — 5 customers, Finance validation and reconciliation
Phase 3: Gradual rollout (6 weeks) — enable by customer segment with monitoring thresholds and rollback playbook
Phase 4: GA and documentation — public API docs, Console help, and internal runbook for Finance/CS
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect adjustments cause revenue recognition issues — Mitigation: require Finance sign-off and QA reconciliation before any live data moves
Risk: Customers perceive smoothing as hidden credits — Mitigation: add explicit invoice line items and customer-facing help text explaining adjustments
Risk: High override rates indicating poor rule tuning — Mitigation: start with conservative defaults and track override metric; schedule tuning sprints
Risk: Edge cases for enterprise contracts — Mitigation: opt-out flag and manual approval by Finance for contract-exempt accounts
open_questions: Q1: Should smoothing be available for annual plan monthly breakdowns or strictly monthly subscriptions? Finance to advise
Q2: What is the maximum allowed cap on cross-account rebalancing for enterprise customers with separate legal entities?
Q3: Is there an accounting preference for amortizing deferred charges vs immediate crediting in ERP?
Q4: Do we need a customer-facing notification email for every smoothing event or only when adjustment exceeds threshold?
notes: This PRD is intentionally conservative: initial rollout limited to non-enterprise linked accounts. Final legal/finance sign-off required before any automatic customer-facing credits are applied. Work with Growth to surface clear UX language to reduce surprise invoices.
